label: input f during original phase (not t=0)
explanation: Sparse token-driven unit: about half of activation mass comes from original-phase steps whose input is f (13.5x lift; never at t=0). Only ~29% of such f steps are active, and magnitude is context-modulated: strongest when the sequence starts with d or v (first_tok d 4.5x, v 3.4x; top examples are almost all d/v-initial with f late in the original phase). Secondary weaker triggers: inputs j, n, p (~4x lift), especially after prev_tok p/g/k, and the <DEL> step (~10% of mass, usually right after an f/j/n). Nearly silent in the copy phase (2% of mass) and at t=0. Adding j/n/p-after-p/g/k raises dev F1 to 0.38 and mass recall to 0.63, but the context dependence is not captured by a simple predicate.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=1 & prev_tok=p (+7.83), t=1 & prev_tok=g (+7.83), t=1 & in_tok=f (+6.29), orig0=d (+4.01), in_tok=j (+3.62), in_tok=p (+3.39). Lower it: prev2_tok=- (-4.41), in_tok=v (-3.64), in_tok=d (-3.46), recall_idx=4 (-3.27).
